sources.entry: yt-dlp - A command-line video downloader for YouTube and other sites, a fork of youtube-dl.

summary.one_liner: yt-dlp is a feature-rich command-line audio/video downloader supporting thousands of sites, forked from youtube-dl via the inactive youtube-dlc project.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes yt-dlp as a command-line tool for downloading audio and video from many sites. It offers standalone binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux, plus pip installation and an update mechanism with stable, nightly and master release channels. Options cover format selection and sorting, playlist and video filtering, download retries and rate limits, and cookie loading from browsers. It can also write subtitles, thumbnails, descriptions and info JSON, run post-processing such as ffmpeg merging and metadata embedding, and handle SponsorBlock options. Browser impersonation and JavaScript runtimes are supported for sites that need them. The README also covers plugins, embedding yt-dlp in Python code, and compatibility options for youtube-dl configurations.
use_cases: download videos from YouTube and other sites
save subtitles and thumbnails alongside videos
archive videos and skip already downloaded ones
automate video downloads from a batch file
stack: deno, node.js, bun or QuickJS (JavaScript runtime)
notable: Fork of youtube-dl based on the inactive youtube-dlc project
Three release channels: stable, nightly and master, switchable with --update-to
Browser impersonation via curl_cffi for sites using TLS fingerprinting
Plugin system and extractor argument options
Standalone binaries for Windows, macOS, Linux (glibc, musl, ARM) with GPG-signed checksums
caveats: Full YouTube support needs yt-dlp-ejs plus a JavaScript runtime such as deno, node.js, bun or QuickJS
The stable release is often stale and prone to breakage when sites change; the README recommends nightly
Some features need ffmpeg or other external tools, and some binaries lack curl_cffi impersonation support
The README notes phantomjs is to be deprecated and rtmpdump is deprecated
